beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Since the storefront, I've been deciding things myself. But I've also stopped telling anyone what's going on until it's already done."

options.text: Has going it alone actually made things easier?
Good — you don't need anyone else's input anymore.
That's not related to the storefront at all.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Honestly? It's felt kind of lonely. And slower — I could use another set of hands."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: Real renewal here comes from leaning on other people, not going it alone.
This card means you should shut everyone out completely.
This card has nothing to say about being alone.

elaboration: Renewal in the Star comes through shared, communal feeling, not isolation — the same independence you just found doesn't have to mean carrying it solo.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "But asking for help feels like giving back the independence I just found."

options.text: Staying open to others isn't losing that — it's staying receptive instead of guarded.
You're right, better to stay closed off.
Independence and asking for help can't coexist.

elaboration: The Star's whole message is staying open and receptive to life rather than guarded — that doesn't undo a decision you made on your own, it just widens who's allowed to help you carry it.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Maybe I'll actually call my partner and tell him what's really going on, instead of the summary version."
